newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer on CenBank dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer on CenBank dlr sales.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly firmer at 495.50/496.50 per dollar Friday as the Central Bank sold foreign currency heavily to defend the bolivar, traders said.
Traders said the Central Bank appeared to be using the currency market as a means to drain excess liquidity on money markets.
"The Central Bank has allowed the exchange rate to slip a lot so that it can sell (foreign currency) at these levels to restrict liquidity," one said.
The bolivar has depreciated by nearly two percent over the last month marking a sharp acceleration in the currency's depreciation rate.
Traders added that reports that the Central Bank may increase its reserve requirement to 17 from 15 percent and led some banks to sell currency to improve their local currency positions.
Traders said the heavy currency sales Friday by the Central Bank had calmed market expectations somewhat and that pressure on the currency may ease slightly.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
